title: HOLISTIC MISSIONS
mv: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
mvp: “And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.” Matthew 25:40
assignment: State five (5) practical ways you can be involved in holistic missions in your daily life (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Holistic missions is a biblical approach to reaching the world for Christ, encompassing both the spiritual and physical needs of humanity. It reflects God's heart for the world, demonstrating His love and care for every aspect of human life. In this lesson, we shall examine the biblical basis, the church's mandate and the components of holistic missions.

In Matthew 25:31-46, Jesus describes the judgement of the nations and great rewards for those who cared for the needy, the hungry, the thirsty, the stranger, the naked, the sick and the prisoner. He equates serving these people with serving Him. This passage highlights the need for holistic missions, where we minister to both the spiritual and physical needs of the people. The early church demonstrated a commitment to holistic missions. In Acts 2:44-45, believers shared their possessions to meet one another's needs. Also, the church in Acts 4:32-35 was characterised by acts of generosity and kindness. James 1:27 defines pure religion as visiting orphans and widows in their troubles and vulnerability. Furthermore, 3 John 2 reveals Apostle John’s desire for the physical well-being as well as the spiritual welfare of the people. Above all, Jesus' ministry was holistic, as He preached the gospel, healed the sick, fed the hungry and comforted the broken-hearted. He demonstrated God's love and care for the whole person, body and soul.

In the same manner, the church has a mandate to preach the gospel to every creature (Mark 16:15) and to care for the physical needs of the people. In Acts 6:1-4, the early church appointed deacons to care for the physical needs of the church, including the widows. This demonstrates the importance of holistic missions in the life of the church.
Evangelism is a crucial component of holistic missions. We are called to share the gospel with people, calling them to repentance and faith in Jesus Christ (Romans 10:9-10).

Discipleship is crucial for effective, holistic missions. It involves teaching people to obey God's commands, nurturing and equipping them to grow and live out their faith in practical ways (2Peter 3:18).
Compassion Ministry is vital in holistic missions as it deals with showing kindness and compassion to people in need, such as the poor, the sick and the vulnerable (Romans 15:26).

Community Development is another important aspect of holistic missions. It involves working to improve the physical and social conditions of communities by providing access to clean water, education, healthcare, etc.
As followers of Christ, we are called to demonstrate God's love and care to transform lives, build godly relationships with people and communities.
